course_profile.one_sentence_summary: An introductory course on data science focusing on similarity search, data stream analysis, link analysis, and frequent itemset mining.
course_profile.short_summary: This course introduces fundamental data science techniques for handling large datasets. Topics include the Bonferroni principle, nearest neighbor search, document shingling, locally sensitive hashing (LSH), various distance measures, data stream filtering and counting (DGIM), PageRank algorithms, and market basket analysis using the Apriori algorithm.

theoretical_understanding: Understand the fundamentals of data analysis and the application of the Bonferroni principle.
Comprehend models for streaming data of varying complexity and link analysis structures.
Understand the mathematical foundations behind similarity preservation in reduced datasets.
practical_implementation: Calculate set similarities using Jaccard, Cosine, Edit, and Hamming distances.
Implement the Apriori algorithm for market basket analysis.
Perform document shingling and locally sensitive hashing for large-scale similarity search.
Calculate standard and topic-sensitive PageRank scores.
analysis_validation: Analyze data streams by filtering elements, performing counts within sliding and decaying windows, and applying the DGIM algorithm.
Identify link spam and evaluate textual similarities to detect plagiarism or mirror pages.
Determine similarities in online purchases and movie ratings.
architecture_design: Design software systems for the efficient filtering of undesirable elements in continuous data streams, such as email spam.
research_and_prototyping: Create predictive and descriptive models for datasets using feature extraction and data generalization techniques.

lab_formats: Laboratory works focused on algorithm implementation and data analysis.
expected_artifacts: Scripts for stream filtering and itemset counting.
implementation_tasks: Implement Jaccard, Cosine, Hamming, and Edit distance calculations.
Build a document shingling and LSH pipeline.
Implement the Apriori algorithm for transaction datasets.
Apply the DGIM algorithm to estimate item counts in a streaming window.
engineering_practices: Algorithmic efficiency optimization for big data.

curricular_relations.reason: Vector math from linear algebra is fundamentally required for computing cosine distance and representing text as vectors.
LSH relies on probabilistic models and hashing collisions to estimate similarities.
Implementing stream filtering and DGIM algorithms requires practical programming capabilities.
Distance measures are directly applied to detect textual similarities, plagiarism, and duplicate documents.

what_student_can_understand: How algorithms process massive, continuous streams of data efficiently without storing everything in memory.
How search engines rank web pages and detect link spam using PageRank.
The mathematical principles behind determining how 'similar' two items (documents, users, transactions) are.
what_student_can_build: Systems for detecting plagiarism or duplicate articles using document shingling.
Email or event stream filtering applications that catch unwanted elements.
Basic recommendation pipelines for online stores using market basket models.
what_student_can_apply: Locally Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for fast similarity searches.
Multiple distance metrics (Jaccard, Cosine, Edit, Hamming).
The Apriori algorithm for finding frequent itemsets.
The DGIM algorithm for windowed counting in data streams.
